clock_and_reset_waveform.SoundWire_Clock_idle_during_clockstop: Parked Low after a 'Stopping Frame' (Master drives all BitSlots of the Stopping Frame, ending with Clock + Data both Low).
clock_and_reset_waveform.SoundWire_Clock_active: Square-wave at 9.6 MHz / 12 MHz / 12.288 MHz typical (13 MHz max for typical geometries; can be faster in single-Slave-close-to-Master configurations).
clock_and_reset_waveform.SoundWire_Data_idle: Held by bus-keeper at last driven level; Modified-NRZI Logic 0 = no change.
clock_and_reset_waveform.POR_release: Power-on reset releases Master to apply Clock and Frame; un-enumerated Slaves wait until 16 consecutive frames of valid static + dynamic sync before declaring 'Attached'.

bit_transfer_waveform.rule: Two BitSlots per Clock period (DDR) — one on the rising edge and one on the falling edge of SoundWire_Clock.
bit_transfer_waveform.encoding: Modified-NRZI: Logic 1 = active level change on the BitSlot boundary; Logic 0 = passive (no change), level held by bus-keeper.
data_handover_cases: Case #1: high-Z → driving (new driver starts; tZD_Data_Min minimum delay after clock edge)
Case #2: driving → driving across two different devices (previous driver tri-states; next driver asserts; momentary tri-state required even if same physical device drives two adjacent BitSlots)
Case #3: driving → high-Z (current driver releases; bus-keeper holds last level)
bit_transfer_waveform.key_constraint: tDZ_Data_Max (worst-case latest time to high-Z) < tZD_Data_Min (worst-case earliest time to drive) so no two drivers fight on a transition.
bit_transfer_waveform.self_timed_turnoff: Permitted self-timed turn-off occurring before the clock edge that ends a given BitSlot; tOH_Data_Min ensures the valid signal is presented long enough for the bus-keeper at the far end of the PCB trace to snap to the new value.
bit_transfer_waveform.figure: Webinar slides 'Data handover (1)/(2)/(3)' and 'Modified NRZI encoding'.

control_word_waveform.position_in_frame: First 48 rows of Column 0 of every Frame (Control Word occupies a 48-row × 1-col strip).
control_word_waveform.static_sync_word: 8 bits plus 1 mode-identification bit (Normal vs High-PHY) — fixed pattern Slaves use to lock onto Frame boundaries; verified for 16 consecutive frames before declaring 'Attached'.
control_word_waveform.dynamic_sync: 4-bit CRC pattern with 15-frame period — removes 'ghost' sync words.
control_word_waveform.ping_status_bits: Three-state per Slave (Not Attached / Attached / Alert), positions for Devices 0..11.
control_word_waveform.command_status: ACK / NAK / Command_Ignored per addressed Slave per Read/Write.
control_word_waveform.parity_bit: Single bit per frame; covers Parity Calculation Window BitSlot[44,1] previous → BitSlot[44,0] current; error may be reported with a 1-frame delay; Slaves do not compute parity until they have successfully synchronized to Master.

frame_shape_waveform.valid_rows_note: Only selected row values in [48, 256] are valid; Master typically uses combinations with rows and columns scaled by 2^N.
frame_shape_waveform.control_word_position: First 48 rows of Col 0 reserved for Control Word; remaining BitSlots carry payload (PCM, PDM, raw DATA).

transport_waveform.sample_event_definition: Instant when data is captured/rendered — word-clock / frame-sync periodic event.
transport_waveform.sample_interval: Number of bits between successive Samples; updates when Frame Shape or sampling frequency changes; not necessarily a multiple of row size; not dependent on number of channels.
transport_waveform.transport_sub_frame: Vertical partition of Frame defined by HStart, HStop (with notional HWidth = HStop - HStart); can also be viewed as a temporal aperture per Data Port.
transport_waveform.payload_data_window: Intersection between Transport Sub-Frame and Payload Data Window (defined by Sample Interval). Can be shared between similar streams.
transport_waveform.block_per_port_mode: All channels of a port packed as a single data chunk per Sample Interval, lowest to highest channel; BlockOffset from start of Payload Data Window.
transport_waveform.block_per_channel_mode: Channels transmitted in individual chunks within same Sample Interval; initial Block_Offset + inter-sample Sub_Block_Offset; benefits: 'holes' in bit allocation reclaimable by other streams.
transport_waveform.grouping: Ability to group up to 4 successive samples to avoid 'vertical stripes' for PDM; required for PDM, optional for PCM.

clockstop_wake_waveform.clockstopnow_then_stopping_frame: Master issues 'ClockStopNow' command in the Control Word, then drives the Stopping Frame (Master owns all BitSlots in the Stopping Frame). Last bit of Stopping Frame parks Data Low; Clock is then held Low.
clockstop_wake_waveform.wake_high_pulse: Wake-Up High for ≥ 2× minimum BitSlot duration on Data; Master then resumes Clock — extended first bit of Frame N+1 followed by the second bit of Frame N+1.

modes.ClockStopMode0: Mandatory; Slave keeps context (registers, Device Number, programmed transport) and restarts immediately on wake.
modes.ClockStopMode1: Optional; Slave may lose context, enters very-low-power mode; Slave needs to be re-enumerated on startup; removes need for extra GPIO for e.g. jack detection.

clockstop_wake_waveform.permission: Master can program which Slaves are allowed to wake the bus.

ssp_waveform.bit_position_in_ping: SSP bit in PING frame; driven at regular intervals.
ssp_waveform.purpose: Maintain alignment between multiple links with different frame rates; between Ports using different sampling rates on the same link; define 'safe' time positions for bus reconfiguration; maintain phase coherence between devices; reset SampleInterval counters and resync transport.
ssp_waveform.constraint: Typically large enough to be multiple of all sample intervals.

monitor_arbitration_waveform.BREQ: Monitor request bit in Control Word; 0 = Master owns, 1 = Monitor requests.
monitor_arbitration_waveform.BREL: Master yield bit in Control Word; 0 = Master keeps, 1 = Master will yield at end of frame.

ownership_truth_table.1_1: Monitor owns; may issue Read/Write commands

enumeration_waveform.step_1: Master applies Clock; programmed Frame Shape is broadcast.
enumeration_waveform.step_2: Slave verifies static + dynamic sync for 16 consecutive frames.
enumeration_waveform.step_3: Slave drives PREQ and/or 'Attached' status bit at Device 0 position in next PING.
enumeration_waveform.step_4: Master issues 6 consecutive READ commands to SCP_Device0..5 of the Slave (still Device Number 0) to read 48-bit enumeration value.
enumeration_waveform.step_5: Master issues WRITE to assign new Device Number 1..11.
enumeration_waveform.step_6: Bus contention: if multiple Slaves report Attached at Device 0, hardware arbitration favors the Slave with the highest 48-bit enumeration value (others back off); Master redoes enumeration until no Slave reports Attached at Device 0.

reset_waveform.hard_reset_power_on: Power-On Reset; Master and Slaves come up at Device Number 0; Interrupt masks disabled; all registers at hardware defaults.
reset_waveform.hard_reset_bus_reset: Master drives 4096 Logic1 transitions on SoundWire_Data; all Slaves perform Hard-Reset.
reset_waveform.hard_reset_device_reset: Master writes Reset bit in SCP_Ctrl of a specific Slave.
reset_waveform.soft_reset: Slave detects two sync errors (not necessarily successive); soft-resets itself; Device Number lost; Interrupt Status register maintained so debug can determine sync-loss cause.

parity_waveform.parity_calculation_window: BitSlot[44,1] of previous frame to BitSlot[44,0] of current frame.
parity_waveform.computation_basis: Physical level read on the bus (not the value sent), so parity detects some bus conflicts as well as bit errors.
parity_waveform.slave_response_on_error: Set NAK bit in current Read/Write Command Status; raise IntStat_Parity interrupt; reported with up to 1-frame delay.
parity_waveform.sync_dependency: Slaves do not compute parity until they have successfully synchronized to Master.
